models._description: Google Service (AbstractModel: generic Google OAuth2 + REST helper, no persisted fields)

behavioral_notes.observation: google.service is an AbstractModel with no fields: it is a parameterized OAuth2 client shared by every Google integration. _get_authorize_uri(service, scope, redirect_uri, state, approval_prompt, access_type) builds the consent URL against https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth with response_type=code and the caller-supplied scope; access_type=offline is what makes Google return a refresh_token. The client_id is read per service from the ir.config_parameter google_<service>_client_id (treated as public, even logged in clear), and the client_secret from google_<service>_client_secret via the module-level _get_client_secret(ICP_sudo, service) hook -- a deliberate indirection so the secret is only ever read inside a request and never returned to a caller in clear. _get_google_tokens(authorize_code, service, redirect_uri) POSTs grant_type=authorization_code to https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token and returns the (access_token, refresh_token, expires_in) tuple; on requests.HTTPError it raises res.config.settings.get_config_warning. _refresh_google_token(service, rtoken) POSTs grant_type=refresh_token to the same token endpoint and returns (access_token, expires_in). None of this token lifecycle is visible from field/model metadata -- the module exposes zero stored fields.

behavioral_notes.element: google.service._do_request (host-allow-listed outbound HTTP wrapper for all Google API calls)
behavioral_notes.observation: _do_request(uri, params, headers, method='POST', preuri=GOOGLE_API_BASE_URL, timeout=20) is the single choke-point through which every downstream Google module makes outbound HTTPS calls (via python-requests). It hard-asserts that the resolved host of preuri+uri is one of the hosts of GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENDPOINT (accounts.google.com) or GOOGLE_API_BASE_URL (www.googleapis.com) -- a static SSRF/host allow-list. GET/DELETE pass params as query string; POST/PATCH/PUT send them as form data with the given headers. It scrubs client_secret from debug logs (first 4 chars + 12 x's), returns a (status, response_json, ask_time) tuple where ask_time is parsed from the response Date header (used by callers for clock-skew-tolerant token-expiry math), maps HTTP 204 to a False body, and swallows 204/404 errors while re-raising every other HTTPError. This generic request/error/redaction behavior is pure code, absent from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: /google_account/authentication public controller (GoogleAuth.oauth2callback) -- shared OAuth2 redirect endpoint
behavioral_notes.observation: The single route (controllers/main.py, type=http auth=public) is the OAuth2 redirect_uri that Google calls back after the user accepts/refuses consent. It JSON-decodes the round-tripped state param into {'s': service, 'f': url_return}, validates that a service is present (and that a code has a return url) else raises BadRequest. On success it reconstructs the redirect_uri from the request url_root, calls google.service._get_google_tokens(code, service, redirect_uri) to exchange the auth code, then dispatches the returned (access_token, refresh_token, ttl) to the current user's res_users_settings_id._set_google_auth_tokens(...) when that field exists (raising if no callback field is defined for the service), and finally redirects back to url_return. On error it appends ?error=<reason> to url_return. The whole module is thus a generic, service-agnostic token broker: it never persists tokens itself; storage and refresh-scheduling live in the downstream module's res.users.settings extension.

behavioral_notes.element: downstream consumption by google_calendar / google_gmail / google_drive (cloud_storage_google)
behavioral_notes.observation: google_account owns no business object and is consumed as shared infrastructure. google_calendar/models/res_users_settings.py defines _set_google_auth_tokens (the callback the controller invokes, persisting google_calendar_rtoken/token/token_validity) and calls google.service._refresh_google_token('calendar', google_calendar_rtoken) to lazily renew an expired access token, wiping the stored tokens on failure. google_gmail/models/google_gmail_mixin.py and cloud_storage_google/models/res_config_settings.py reuse the same google_<service>_client_id/google_<service>_client_secret ICP convention and the /google_account/authentication callback, though google_gmail hand-builds its own oauth2/v2/auth consent URL rather than calling _get_authorize_uri. The per-service 'service' string ('calendar', 'gmail', 'drive', ...) is the parameter that lets one generic google.service serve every integration with distinct client credentials and scopes.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration -> Google OAuth2 + Google APIs (gap #7, static)
behavioral_notes.observation: Outbound HTTPS integration via python-requests to Google, host allow-listed by assertion in google.service._do_request to accounts.google.com (oauth2 auth + token endpoints) and www.googleapis.com (all Google REST APIs reached by downstream modules). The OAuth2 client_id (google_<service>_client_id ICP, public, in clear) and client_secret (google_<service>_client_secret ICP, never returned in clear, scrubbed from logs) are admin-supplied per Google Cloud project/service. No vendored SDK -- the OAuth2/REST client is hand-rolled in models/google_service.py with a 20s timeout. This external SaaS dependency (Google identity + APIs) is invisible to Python model/field metadata and is the defining trait of the module.

classification.rationale: google_account is shared OAuth2/identity infrastructure: it owns no business object (a single AbstractModel google.service with zero persisted fields, no security groups, no views) and produces no sellable output. It is the generic Google OAuth2 + REST plumbing -- consent-URL building, authorization-code exchange, refresh-token renewal and a host-allow-listed outbound request wrapper -- on which google_calendar, google_gmail and google_drive (cloud_storage_google) build by supplying a per-service 'service' string and google_<service>_client_id/secret credentials. Per Stabell & Fjeldstad this is a support / firm-infrastructure function (activity_class=support). For APQC it maps to 8.0 Manage Information Technology -- specifically the external-system-integration / credential-lifecycle band: the module's entire reason to exist is third-party SaaS integration (gap #7: it talks to accounts.google.com and www.googleapis.com) and OAuth2 credential management, which are IT-management concerns rather than business-capability development. This mirrors its sibling microsoft_account (and matches the 8.0 classification of the downstream google_calendar / microsoft_calendar connectors): the parent capability modules own their business capability (scheduling, mail, files); this base owns the IT identity/token plumbing that integrates those capabilities with Google. 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was rejected because nothing here develops a new business capability -- it operates an external authentication interface; 9.0 'Acquire, Construct, and Manage Assets' was rejected since no physical/IT asset is managed, only API credentials and an OAuth2 token exchange.

standard_capabilities: generic Google OAuth2 authorization-code flow reusable by any Google service (calendar/gmail/drive)
access_type=offline consent so Google returns a long-lived refresh_token
authorization-code -> token exchange and refresh-token renewal against accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token
single public OAuth2 redirect callback (/google_account/authentication) that dispatches tokens to the right downstream store
per-service client id/secret configuration via ir.config_parameter (google_<service>_client_id / client_secret)
host-allow-listed, secret-redacting outbound HTTP wrapper (_do_request) for all Google API traffic
typical_fits: downstream Google modules (calendar, gmail, drive) reusing one OAuth2 base instead of each re-implementing the flow
self-registered Google Cloud project: admin sets client id/secret per service in Settings
tokens persisted and refreshed by the consuming module on res.users.settings, not by this base
common_gaps: no token storage / no res.users(.settings) fields of its own -- every consuming module must implement _set_google_auth_tokens and its own *_rtoken/token/token_validity fields
no built-in UI: client id/secret config and any connect button live in base_setup / the downstream module
no automatic refresh scheduling -- _refresh_google_token must be invoked lazily by the caller on expiry
google_gmail hand-builds its own oauth2/v2/auth consent URL rather than calling _get_authorize_uri (inconsistent reuse)
single-project credentials per service; no multi-tenant / per-company client credential isolation
no token-revocation endpoint call -- 'disconnect' is handled by the downstream module wiping its stored tokens

open_questions: Exact set of downstream 'service' strings in production (calendar / gmail / drive) and which still route their callback through /google_account/authentication vs a module-local one.
Whether google_gmail's bespoke oauth2/v2/auth consent URL (bypassing _get_authorize_uri) is intentional divergence or a candidate for consolidation onto google.service.
How clock skew is handled across services: ask_time is parsed from the Google Date header in _do_request, but token-validity math lives in each downstream res.users.settings.
